response.summary: The revised plan text resolves R2-F1 and R2-F2: day edges now apply only where both the media strip range and the container width allow seven columns, and only to non-selected days, and the 4.5:1 contrast requirement is stated. The F1–F7 resolutions from round 1 are still in place. The remaining defects are in the verification evidence, not the design. surfaces.cjs now exists, and the plan names it as the proof for several commitments it does not yet check. It never compares day-column count with day borders at any width or text size. Its sheet-versus-ground L* check reads `body` backgroundColor rather than the ground actually rendered behind the ledger, so it can pass when it shouldn't. Its contrast check samples one `.quiet` element on the rail and nothing else. There is also a small range gap between the existing `max-width:36rem` container query and the planned `min-width:36.0625rem` complement.

findings.evidence: Decision 6 says: 'surfaces.cjs must compare the actual day-column count with day borders at 1366/1048/800/700/390/320 at 100/200%.' The script reads `.day` only once (line 12, via `document.querySelector`, which returns the first day). That read is at 1048px and 100% text, it is not compared with `.days` gridTemplateColumns, and nothing asserts on it. The separator loop (line 14) reads only `.desk-side` and the session, and never sets root text to 200%. A regression where list-mode days get #bcc4b5 edges, or the selected day loses its charcoal edge, would therefore pass. This is the exact failure R2-F1 was about.
findings.fix: Add a loop over [1366,1048,800,700,390,320] × [100%,200%] root font size. At each step, count the rendered columns in `.days` (e.g. `getComputedStyle(.days).gridTemplateColumns.split(' ').length`, or distinct `offsetTop`s of `.day`). Read borderTopColor for a non-selected day and for `[aria-selected=true]`. Assert: #bcc4b5 (rgb(188,196,181)) if and only if columns===7; transparent for non-selected days in list mode; the selected day stays rgb(19,23,24).

findings.evidence: Line 13 computes `sheetGroundLstar` and `railGroundLstar` from `s.body.backgroundColor`. The plan says to 'record actual rendered ground at the sheet position… do not rely only on a declared top gradient token.' The ground may be painted on `html:has(...)` with `body` left transparent, which decision 2 allows. In that case `body.backgroundColor` is `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`. `rgb()` then parses it as 0,0,0, L* comes out as 0, and the ≥4 assertion passes trivially, as does `notEqual(ledger, body)`. If instead the top light were a long gradient on `backgroundImage`, it would never be measured at all.
findings.fix: Sample the rendered pixel. Take a page screenshot clip a few px outside the ledger's bounding box (e.g. 8px to its left, or in the `.desk-lower` gap) and one inside the ledger. Compute L* from those pixels. Also sample just outside `.desk-side` for the rail-versus-ground value. At minimum, assert that html or body has a non-transparent background and use whichever is painted.

findings.evidence: The risks section requires 'computed muted/metadata/text-button foreground contrast against its actual rail/ground/sheet parent; 4.5:1 minimum'. Line 13 checks only `document.querySelector('.quiet')`, which is the session's 'Eastern time', against `.desk-side`. These go unchecked: `.message-meta time`, `.count` and the `.text-button`/`.head-link` colours in the rail; `.day-name`/`.day-note` and the calendar `.quiet` date range on the frameless calendar, which sits over the Home ground; and `.work-meta`/`.ledger-no` (#6c7469) on the sheet and on the #eceee7 current-row wash.
findings.fix: Sample each of those selectors inside its scope (e.g. `.desk-side time`, `.desk-side .count`, `.week .quiet`, `.week .day-name`, `.ledger .work-meta`, `.ledger .is-current .work-meta`, `.ledger-no`, `.text-button`). Resolve the nearest non-transparent ancestor background (ground pixel for `.week`), and assert ≥4.5:1 for each.

findings.evidence: The existing list-mode query is `@container(max-width:36rem)` (line 464). The planned strip-edge condition is `min-width:36.0625rem`. That leaves a gap from 576 to 577px at 100% text, and from 1152 to 1154px at 200%. Container widths are often fractional because `.desk-lower` uses fr tracks and clamp padding. At a width in that gap, the media rule has already made seven columns, but neither container rule applies, so the strip renders without the new edges.
findings.fix: Use range syntax, `@container (width > 36rem)`, or `@container not (max-width:36rem)`. Either is the exact complement of the existing query.

coverage: Re-checked R2-F1 and R2-F2 against decision 6 and the risks section of the revised plan. Both are addressed in the plan text.

Read surfaces.cjs in full and compared its assertions with the plan's stated proofs: subpage before/after styles, DOM and card counts, surface roles, L*, contrast, separator directions, and saved-preview and read states.

Checked the separator loop's width expectations (1920/1366/800/390/320 horizontal; 1100/1048/700 vertical) against the existing `.desk-side` media rules at style.css lines 170, 386, 408, 421 and 426. They match.
Re-checked the existing `@container(max-width:36rem)` and media strip rules (style.css 384-473) against the planned min-width complement.
Listed the home-surface-20261026 evidence folder (before renders, surfaces-before.json, scripts, earlier plan-review runs).
limitations: I couldn't run surfaces.cjs or the other Playwright/Edge scripts, and I didn't open surfaces-before.json or the before PNGs.
There is no implementation yet. This review covers the plan and the diagnostic script against the current stylesheet.
I didn't read capture-11.cjs, calendar-internal.cjs or interactions.cjs in this round. Their stated case counts are taken from the plan.
The contrast and L* reasoning comes from hand calculation and source reading, not rendered measurement.
